# PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM

## General

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > General] 1. Subject to the following provisions of this practice direction, proceedings where both the High Court and the County Court have jurisdiction may be started in the High Court or in the County Court.

## Where to start proceedings

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Where to start proceedings] 2.1 Proceedings (whether for damages or for a specified sum) may only be started in the High Court if the value of the claim is more than £100,000.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Where to start proceedings] 2.2 Proceedings which include a claim for damages in respect of personal injuries may only be started in the High Court if the value of the claim is £50,000 or more (paragraph 9 of the High Court and County Courts Jurisdiction Order 1991 (S.I. 1991/724 as amended) describes how the value of a claim is to be determined).

## 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] 2.4 Subject to paragraphs 2.1 and 2.2 above, a claim should be started in the High Court if by reason of—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] (1) the financial value of the claim and the amount in dispute, and/or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] (2) the complexity of the facts, legal issues, remedies or procedures involved, and/or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] (3) the importance of the outcome of the claim to the public in general,the claimant believes that the claim ought to be dealt with by a High Court judge.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] (CPR Part 30 and Practice Direction 30 contain provisions relating to the transfer to the County Court of proceedings started in the High Court and vice-versa.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] 2.5 (1) A claim in the County Court under Part 7 may be made at any County Court hearing centre, unless any enactment, rule or practice direction provides otherwise.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] (2) If a claim which is required to be made at a particular County Court hearing centre is made at the wrong hearing centre, a court officer will send the claim to the correct hearing centre before it is issued.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] 2.6 A claim relating to Business and Property work (which includes any of the matters specified in paragraph 1 of Schedule 1 to the Senior Courts Act 1981) and which includes any work under the jurisdiction of the Business and Property Courts, may, subject to any enactment, rule or practice direction, be dealt with in the High Court or in the County Court. The claim form should, if issued in the High Court, be marked in the top right hand corner ‘Business and Property Courts’ and, if issued in the County Court, be marked ‘Business and Property work’ (except, in the County Court, for those areas listed as exceptions in paragraph 4.2 of Practice Direction 57AA (Business and Property Courts).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] (For the equity jurisdiction of the County Court, see section 23 of the County Courts Act 1984.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] 2.7 A claim relating to any of the matters specified in sub-paragraphs (a) and (b) of paragraph 2 of Schedule 1 to the Senior Courts Act 1981 must be dealt with in the High Court and will be assigned to the King’s Bench Division.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] 2.8 Practice directions applying to particular types of proceedings, or to proceedings in particular courts, will contain provisions relating to the commencement and conduct of those proceedings.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] 2.9 The following proceedings may not be started in the County Court unless the parties have agreed otherwise in writing—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] (1) a claim for damages or other remedy for libel or slander, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.3 A claim must be issued in the High Court or the County Court if an enactment so requires.] (2) a claim in which the title to any toll, fair, market or franchise is in question.

## 2.10

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.10] (1) Subject to paragraph 2.9, a claim relating to media and communications work (which includes any work which would fall within the jurisdiction of the Media and Communications List if issued in the High Court) may be started in the County Court or High Court; and paragraph 2.1 shall not apply to such a claim.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.10] (2) Such a claim should be started in the High Court if, by reason of the factors set out in paragraph 2.4(1) to (3), the claimant believes that the claim ought to be dealt with by a High Court judge.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.10] (3) If a claimant starts such a claim in the High Court and the court decides that it should have been started in the County Court, the court will normally transfer it to the County Court on its own initiative. This is likely to result in delay.

## 2.11

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.11] (1) The normal rules apply in deciding in which court and specialist list a claim that includes issues under the Human Rights Act 1998 should be started. They also apply in deciding which procedure to use to start the claim; this Part or CPR Part 8 or CPR Part 54 (judicial review).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.11] (2) The exception is a claim for damages in respect of a judicial act, which should be started in the High Court. If the claim is made in a notice of appeal then it will be dealt with according to the normal rules governing where that appeal is heard.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 2.11] (The County Court cannot make a declaration of incompatibility in accordance with section 4 of the Human Rights Act 1998. Legislation may direct that such a claim is to be brought before a specified tribunal.)

## The claim form

## 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] 3.2 Other practice directions may require other forms to be used to start types of proceedings, or proceedings in particular courts.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] 3.3 Where a claim form to be served out of the jurisdiction is one which the court has power to deal with under—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] (a) the Civil Jurisdiction and Judgments Act 1982; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] (b) the Judgments Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 1215/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 December 2012 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters), the claim form must, under rule 6.34, be filed and served with the notice referred to in that rule and paragraph 2.1 of Practice Direction 6B.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] 3.4 If a claim for damages or for an unspecified sum is started in the High Court, the claim form must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] (1) state that the claimant expects to recover more than £100,000 (or £50,000 or more if the claim is for personal injuries); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] (2) state that some enactment provides that the claim may only be started in the High Court and specify that enactment; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] (3) state that the claim is to be in one of the specialist High Court lists (see CPR Parts 49 and 58–62) and specify that list.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] 3.5 If a claim for damages for personal injuries is started in the County Court, the claim form must state whether or not the claimant expects to recover more than £1000 in respect of pain, suffering and loss of amenity.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] 3.6 If a claim for housing disrepair which includes a claim for an order requiring repairs or other work to be carried out by the landlord is started in the County Court, the claim form must state—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] (1) whether or not the cost of the repairs or other work is estimated to be more than £1000, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] (2) whether or not the claimant expects to recover more than £1000 in respect of any claim for damages.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 3.1 A claimant must use form N1 to start a claim under Part 7.] If either of the amounts mentioned in (1) and (2) is more than £1000, the small claims track will not be the normal track for that claim.

## Title of proceedings

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Title of proceedings] 4.1 The claim form and every other statement of case, must be headed with the title of the proceedings. The title should state—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Title of proceedings] (1) the identifying number given to the proceedings;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Title of proceedings] (2) the court or Division in which they are proceeding;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Title of proceedings] (3) the full name of each party;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Title of proceedings] (4) each party’s status in the proceedings (i.e. claimant/defendant).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Title of proceedings] (Paragraph 2.4 of Practice Direction 16 sets out what is meant by a full name in respect of each type of claimant.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Title of proceedings] 4.2 Where there is more than one claimant and/or more than one defendant, the parties should be described in the title as follows—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Title of proceedings] 1.  [Name of first claimant] 2.  [Name of second claimant, etc] and 1.  [Name of first defendant] 2.  [Name of second defendant, etc]

## Starting a Part 7 Claim in the County Court

## 5.1 (1) Subject to subparagraph (2), if a claim—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 5.1 (1) Subject to subparagraph (2), if a claim—] (a) is started in the County Court under Part 7;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 5.1 (1) Subject to subparagraph (2), if a claim—] (b) is a claim only for an amount of money, whether specified or unspecified; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 5.1 (1) Subject to subparagraph (2), if a claim—] (c) is not a claim for which special procedures are provided in the Civil Procedure Rules or practice directions, form N1 must be sent to: Civil National Business Centre, St Katharine’s House, 21-27 St Katharine’s Street, Northampton, NN1 2LH, DX 702885 Northampton 7.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 5.1 (1) Subject to subparagraph (2), if a claim—] (2) For the purpose of this practice direction, the procedure in Practice Direction 49D is not a special procedure.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 5.1 (1) Subject to subparagraph (2), if a claim—] 5.2 In proceedings referred to in paragraph 4A.1, the claimant must specify the preferred hearing centre on form N1.

## Start of proceedings

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Start of proceedings] 6.1 Proceedings are started when the court issues a claim form at the request of the claimant (see rule 7.2) but where the claim form as issued was received in the court office on a date earlier than the date on which it was issued by the court, the claim is “brought” for the purposes of the Limitation Act 1980 and any other relevant statute on that earlier date.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Start of proceedings] 6.2 The date on which the claim form was received by the court will be recorded by a date stamp either on the claim form held on the court file or on the letter that accompanied the claim form when it was received by the court.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Start of proceedings] 6.3 An enquiry about the date on which the claim form was received by the court should be directed to a court officer.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Start of proceedings] 6.4 Parties proposing to start a claim which is approaching the expiry of the limitation period should recognise the potential importance of establishing the date the claim form was received by the court and should themselves make arrangements to record the date.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Start of proceedings] 6.5 Where a person seeks to start proceedings against the estate of a deceased defendant where probate or letters of administration have not been granted, the claimant should issue the claim against “the personal representatives of A.B. deceased”. The claimant should then, before the expiry of the period for service of the claim form, apply to the court for the appointment of a person to represent the estate of the deceased.

## Claims by and against partnerships within the jurisdiction

## 7.1 Paragraphs 7 and 8 apply to claims that are brought by or against two or more persons who—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 7.1 Paragraphs 7 and 8 apply to claims that are brought by or against two or more persons who—] (1) were business partners; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 7.1 Paragraphs 7 and 8 apply to claims that are brought by or against two or more persons who—] (2) carried on that partnership business within the jurisdiction, at the time when the cause of action accrued.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 7.1 Paragraphs 7 and 8 apply to claims that are brought by or against two or more persons who—] 7.2 For the purposes of this paragraph, “partners” includes persons claiming to be entitled as partners and persons alleged to be partners.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 7.1 Paragraphs 7 and 8 apply to claims that are brought by or against two or more persons who—] 7.3 Where that partnership has a name, unless it is inappropriate to do so, claims must be brought in or against the name under which that partnership carried on business at the time the cause of action accrued.

## Partnership membership statements

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Partnership membership statements] 8.1 In this paragraph a ‘partnership membership statement’ is a written statement of the names and last known places of residence of all the persons who were partners in the partnership at the time when the cause of action accrued, being the date specified for this purpose in accordance with paragraph 8.3.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Partnership membership statements] 8.2 If the partners are requested to provide a copy of a partnership membership statement by any party to a claim, the partners must do so within 14 days of receipt of the request.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Partnership membership statements] 8.3 In that request the party seeking a copy of a partnership membership statement must specify the date when the relevant cause of action accrued.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Partnership membership statements] (Signing of the acknowledgment of service in the case of a partnership is dealt with in CPR rule 10.5(5).)

## Persons carrying on business in another name

## 9.1 This paragraph applies where—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 9.1 This paragraph applies where—] (1) a claim is brought against an individual;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 9.1 This paragraph applies where—] (2) that individual carries on a business within the jurisdiction (even if not personally within the jurisdiction); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 9.1 This paragraph applies where—] (3) that business is carried on in a name other than that individual’s own name (“the business name”).

## 9.2 The claim may be brought against the business name as if it were the name of a partnership.

## Statement of truth

## 10.1 The form of a statement of truth is specified in paragraph 2.1 of Practice Direction 22.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 10.1 The form of a statement of truth is specified in paragraph 2.1 of Practice Direction 22.] 10.2 Attention is drawn to rule 32.14 which sets out the consequences of verifying a statement of case containing a false statement without an honest belief in its truth.

## Extension of time

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > Extension of time] 11.1 An application under rule 7.6 (for an extension of time for serving a claim form under rule 7.6(1)) must be made in accordance with Part 23 and supported by evidence.

## 11.2 The evidence should state—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 11.2 The evidence should state—] (1) all the circumstances relied on,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 11.2 The evidence should state—] (2) the date of issue of the claim,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 11.2 The evidence should state—] (3) the expiry date of any rule 7.6 extension, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 11.2 The evidence should state—] (4) a full explanation as to why the claim has not been served.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 7A – HOW TO START PROCEEDINGS – THE CLAIM FORM > 11.2 The evidence should state—] (For information regarding (1) written evidence see Part 32 and Practice Direction 32 and (2) service of the claim form see Part 6 and Practice Directions 6A and 6B.)
